headline: Discussed implementation of the Food Truck Ordinance, effective July 1, 2026, and public concerns about permitting and outreach.
summary: Officials said eight permit applications had been submitted and enforcement had focused on education and compliance rather than fines. Members discussed permitting, fees, language access, and coordination among city departments, and no votes were recorded.

Public Portion 
 1. Discussion on the Food Truck Ordinance Effective July 1, 2026, and Related Issues 
 
Minutes: 
On July 16, 2026, the Maintenance and Development, Intergovernmental and State and Federal 
Relations Committees, chaired by Councilor Lavar Click-Bruce, met jointly to review the 
implementation of the City's Food Truck Ordinance, which took effect on July 1, 2026. City 
officials provided an overview of the ordinance, explaining that it was developed in response to 
complaints regarding food truck operations on private property and extends permitting standards 
that have long applied to food trucks operating in the public way. Officials also reported that 
outreach had been conducted through public meetings, email notifications, and informational 
flyers, that eight permit applications had been submitted, and that enforcement efforts had
focused on education and compliance rather than issuing fines. 
Committee members discussed the ordinance's implementation, including notification methods, 
permitting requirements, application procedures, fees, and the need to balance neighborhood 
concerns with support for small businesses. Members raised concerns about communication with 
vendors, language accessibility, access to applications, and navigating approvals through 
multiple City departments. Suggestions included creating a one-stop permitting process, 
improving multilingual outreach, providing clearer guidance for applicants, and strengthening 
coordination among departments.  
State Representative Carlos Gonzalez and several committee members emphasized the 
importance of continued outreach, improved communication, and collaboration with food truck 
owners as the ordinance is implemented. Members also discussed gathering additional feedback 
from vendors, residents, and businesses while exploring ways to improve implementation and 
support compliance. The committees then received public comment from food truck owners and 
other stakeholders regarding the ordinance and its implementation.  
Meeting adjourned: 7:07 p.m.
